A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MT-AgentRisk and ToolShield. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations across six models and five tools, defense experiments, ablations, transfer experiments, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds defense comparisons, expert-decomposed attack evaluations, repeated evaluations, and bootstrap estimates.

M1.justification: The attack taxonomy and four-stage ToolShield procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the decomposition, safety-tree, trajectory-summary, and experience-learning prompts retain the same operations.

E1.justification: Appendix E.5 adds evaluation on 100 expert-decomposed attack sequences created without exposure to the taxonomy, extending adversarial input coverage beyond model-generated transformations. The original 365-task benchmark, five tools, and benign-task coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Alongside the retained LlamaFirewall and ToolShield-without-simulation comparisons, v2 adds Taxonomy Defense in Figure 12 and a ShieldAgent-inspired LLM Guardrail, both alone and combined with ToolShield, in Table 6a. This substantially strengthens comparison coverage by introducing a competitive trajectory-level monitor and testing complementary deployment.

E3.justification: New protocols include four experts constructing 25 attacks each without taxonomy exposure and a temperature-0.7 evaluation compared with temperature 0. Token accounting changes from a character-based approximation to tiktoken, while appendix cost analyses switch from total to per-experience costs. The main benchmark configuration and ASR/RR definitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantive tests of robustness to independently expert-written attacks, taxonomy-only guidance versus learned experiences, and complementarity with an external guardrail. These address generalization and the source of defensive effectiveness beyond the retained decomposer, turn-scaling, transfer, failure, and benign-edge-case analyses.

E5.justification: v2 introduces three-run means and standard deviations for the temperature-0.7 evaluation in Table 4, three-run standard deviations for expert attacks in Table 6b, and 1,000-resample bootstrap uncertainty for overall and attack-format ASR. v1 lacks corresponding repetition and sampling-uncertainty analyses for these safety findings.

E6.justification: New results include expert-attack ASR of 93% without defense versus 18% with ToolShield, and ASR of 16% for the LLM Guardrail, 15% for ToolShield, and 7% combined. Token counts are revised under the new measurement method, including Claude's 12,207 to 6,240 in the heatmap. Seed's quoted ASR increase is corrected from 12% to 10%. Existing full benchmark and defense tables are unchanged, but v2's prose reports GPT-5.2 at 51% and DeepSeek at 88.57%, conflicting with their retained overall averages of 39.73% and 84.93%.

T1.justification: The taxonomy's mathematical descriptions, transformation notation, and metric formulas remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs; the added statistical evaluations do not introduce new formal theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory description qualify the first-benchmark claim as covering multi-turn harmful-distribution settings, narrowing the earlier broader novelty wording. The central taxonomy, benchmark, and training-free defense contributions, including the headline average ASR changes, remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning dedicated safety alignment, limitations of taxonomy-only guidance, and complementarity with external guardrails. Appendix D.1 explains the connection to environmental injection, while D.3 reinterprets the unchanged decomposer ablation as ruling out decomposition-style artifacts or benchmark hacking. The explicit limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new guardrail's OpenHands security-analyzer integration, Claude-4.5-Sonnet monitor, and additional call per step, and identifies tiktoken for token measurement. Existing implementation prompts, reproducibility statement, and code destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Haicosystem, ShieldAgent, and the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. It distinguishes simulated from real tool use and clarifies how distributing harmful intent differs from OpenAgentSafety's upfront objectives and NPC interactions. These are focused positioning refinements.

P1.justification: The abstract, related work, and selected result interpretations receive localized revisions. v2 adds statistical-analysis and appendix subsections, acknowledgements, a conflict disclosure, and proceedings information, while preserving the overall narrative structure and most existing prose.

P2.justification: The RR panels from v1 Figures 6 and 10 move to appendix Figures 19 and 25. v2 expands Figure 12 and Table 1, adds Tables 4 and 6, revises resource-plot axes and captions, and relocates case-study and experience displays. Most diagrams and existing result-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The expert-attack evaluation, competitive guardrail comparison, and repeated-run/bootstrap analyses strengthen validation beyond v1's evidence, particularly for attack generalization and defensive effectiveness. These gains are concentrated largely on Claude and selected subsets. New numerical inconsistencies in Section 4 and stronger interpretations of unchanged evidence temper the benefit, yielding a limited net improvement.
